rationale: All three of my round-3 advisories are ADDRESSED at ad66efbc (classifications in findings), the eight AC-5 legs are mutually consistent, runnable, and red-on-revert (I verified the seams both new legs depend on: SetMergeMetadataForTest at migrate.go and the EnsureMigrated backfill; the nine-writer inventory sites spec.go:76/:84, impl.go, adopt.go:424, complete.go:1366, release.go:152 all check out), and the nine-writer scope propagation into In Scope and Impacted Domains is clean and mutually consistent. But the regression scan ordered for this round surfaced one defect that four rounds of review missed, and I verified it against the tree rather than inferring it: R1.3's agreement table carries TWO rows that are unsatisfiable against the derivation surface the requirement itself names ('DerivePhaseFromChildren over the fixture's child set'). (1) The 'complete → plan (remaining beads all blocked)' leg: I read advanceState (complete.go:1429-1457) — NextMode is exactly DerivePhaseFromChildren's output, and for a mid-spec fixture with one closed bead and remaining blocked beads, lifecycleClosed ≥ 1 forces IMPLEMENT (derive.go's some-closed branch; blocked counts as neither closed nor in_progress), with advanceState returning (implement, "") when nothing is bd-ready. ModePlan post-complete is reachable only via the EMPTY-lifecycle-set fallback (derive.go's spec-095 lifecycleTotal==0 branch — e.g. completing a non-lifecycle follow-up child) or via a swallowed FetchChildren error ('children, _ :=' yields an empty set → plan). The row's stated canonical state derives a different mode than the row asserts, so AC-2's fixture for that leg is red-forever as conditioned. (2) The 'impl approve/impl adopt → idle' rows: an all-closed child set makes DerivePhaseFromChildren return REVIEW — idle comes from the closed epic status / the stored 'done' write, which lives outside the named pure function. Both defects are one-clause fixes (re-condition the plan leg; name the status-aware derivation as the third surface or add per-row carve-outs), but the agreement table is R1's core deliverable and the gate standard for this round is grounded/falsifiable/consistent — a table row whose fixture obligation is unsatisfiable as written fails two of the three, so I cannot honestly approve with it standing.
concrete_changes_required: R1.3, complete row: re-condition the `plan` leg. 'Remaining beads all blocked' derives IMPLEMENT (derive.go some-closed branch: blocked is neither closed nor in_progress, and the just-closed bead makes lifecycleClosed ≥ 1; advanceState then returns implement with an empty next bead). The states that actually reach FormatResult's ModePlan branch are (a) the empty-lifecycle-set fallback (DerivePhaseFromChildren's lifecycleTotal==0 branch, spec 095 — completing a non-lifecycle follow-up child of an epic with no lifecycle children), and (b) a swallowed FetchChildren error in advanceState (children, _ := — empty set derives plan). Condition the leg on (a), and give (b) a disposition — it is a discovery-failure-serialized-as-mode instance of exactly the class R2.3/R1.4 exist to fix, so either fold it into R2's scope explicitly or record the deferral.

R1.3 / AC-2, impl approve + impl adopt rows: the named derivation surface (DerivePhaseFromChildren over the fixture's child set) returns `review` for an all-closed child set, not `idle` — idle is determined by the closed epic status / stored `done`, outside that function. Either name the status-aware derivation (DerivePhaseWithStatus-class, which handles the closed-epic case) as the table's derivation surface for all rows, or add the terminal rows' carve-out stating the derivation surface is epic-status-determined there. As written, AC-2's three-surface assertion for those rows is unsatisfiable.

Optional but adjacent (one sentence, plan-time disposition acceptable): FormatResult's ModePlan branch text 'Remaining beads are blocked. Mode: plan' (complete.go:1396-1400) mischaracterizes both of its actually-reachable trigger states — the spec inherited that message's framing into the table row. Since R2 owns result-message honesty for `complete`, note that the chosen re-conditioning of the table row should flow into that message's text so the row and the message agree.

findings.title: Agreement-table rows unsatisfiable against the named derivation surface: complete→plan mis-conditioned; impl-approve/adopt→idle derives review
findings.detail: Verified at the reviewed commit. (1) advanceState (complete.go:1429-1457) sets NextMode to DerivePhaseFromChildren's output directly; for the row's stated state — mid-spec, remaining beads all blocked — the just-closed bead gives lifecycleClosed ≥ 1 and blocked children count as open, so derivation returns IMPLEMENT (derive.go:379-384) and advanceState returns (implement, "") when bd ready is empty. NextMode=plan post-complete is reachable only when lifecycleTotal == 0 (derive.go's spec-095 empty-set fallback) or when FetchChildren errors and the swallowed error leaves an empty child set. R1.3's 'complete → plan (remaining beads all blocked — FormatResult's ModePlan branch)' therefore asserts a mode its own stated fixture cannot derive; AC-2's fixture for that leg is unsatisfiable, and the parenthetical inherits FormatResult's mischaracterized message text rather than the reachable condition. (2) For the impl approve/impl adopt → idle rows, the all-closed child set makes the named pure function return REVIEW; idle is epic-status/stored-done-determined, outside DerivePhaseFromChildren. The row set and the surface definition cannot both stand: either the derivation surface becomes the status-aware derivation for all rows, or the terminal rows get an explicit carve-out. Both fixes are one clause each, but the table is R1's core deliverable — a row that enshrines a wrong claim defeats the table's anti-drift purpose, which is why this is MAJOR rather than MINOR despite its size.

findings.title: Swallowed FetchChildren error in advanceState is a discovery-failure-as-mode instance the spec's own subject covers
findings.detail: advanceState's 'children, _ := phase.FetchChildren(epicID)' converts a bd failure into an empty child set, which derives plan — so a transient Dolt outage during complete's step 6 produces 'Mode: plan' guidance (and, via complete.go:1366's sync, potentially a stored-phase write computed from a failure). This is the same failure-serialized-as-answer class as R1.4's {"mode": ""} and R2.3's indeterminate-vs-idle collapse, discovered while verifying the table row. It needs only a disposition (fold into R2's scope or record the deferral), not necessarily new mechanism — recorded so it is chartered rather than rediscovered.

findings.title: Regression scan of the changed AC surface: clean apart from the MAJOR above
findings.detail: AC-5's eight legs are mutually consistent and individually runnable: (i)-(iv) unchanged and red today; (v) grounded on same-process flock contention (verified round 3); (vi) is the mechanized inventory obligation with a sensible spec-side/plan-side split; (vii) is runnable — SetMergeMetadataForTest exists (migrate.go, verified) and the under-lock absent-check-re-runs-and-no-ops semantics are coherent with EnsureMigrated writing only when stored phase is absent; (viii) is correctly conditional on the redesign leg, and its interaction with legs (i)-(ii) is covered by (i)'s warning-absent disjunct (under the redesign leg the release route no longer produces the mismatch, which is the point) plus the fixture being directly constructed. AC-2's extended carve-out branch matches R1.3's row text exactly, including the redesign-leg variant. The nine-writer propagation is internally consistent across R3.3, In Scope, and Impacted Domains, with the spec.go:84 creation-seed exclusion carrying a correct rationale (no stored value exists to race at creation). AC-10's positional-emit-only exception is coherent with R6.3(a)'s documented exclusion and leaves AC-10b untouched. The ADR-0023 :142→:141 all-open-row correction matches the file (implement row and all-open row adjacent at :140-:141, verified).
